item.title: COFINA bondholder case against insurers is set back
item.description: A federal judge dismissed a case against Ambac Financial, Ambac Assurance, National Public Finance Guarantee and MBIA Insurance but allowed the case against MBIA Inc. to continue.

item.title: Fed's Goolsbee: Prioritize inflation before further cuts
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said the central bank should focus on getting inflation to its 2% target before making any additional cuts to short-term interest rates.

item.title: Oklahoma Supreme Court to rule on utilities' winter storm bonds
item.description: Appeals challenging authorization for $1.45 billion of ratepayer-backed bonds sold in the wake of a 2021 winter storm are in the hands of the high court.

item.title: Counties frustrated as FEMA reform stalls
item.description: A bill that would change the rules for handling natural disasters is stalled in Congress as county governments grapple with the Federal Emergency Management Agency's regulations.

item.title: Plano cancels ballot vote on leaving Dallas transit agency
item.description: Plano is the first of six Dallas Area Rapid Transit member cities to cancel a May 2 election to drop out of the agency, while others could follow suit.

item.title: Nixon Peabody promotes Eric Brenner to counsel
item.description: The Albany-based lawyer specializes in conduit financing.

item.title: Cook: AI's labor impact may take years to measure
item.description: Federal Reserve Gov. Lisa Cook said AI could boost productivity, but warned the transition may raise unemployment and force difficult tradeoffs between inflation and jobs.

item.title: BAM hires Philip Moos to join its muni capital markets team
item.description: Moos, who was most recently a managing director of municipal bond sales at Wells Fargo, will report to Bryan Baebler, BAM's head of municipal capital markets.

item.title: Amid D.C. sewer line leak, water utilities push for more SRF funds
item.description: The drinking and clean water state revolving fund programs and other water infrastructure programs are up for reauthorization this year.

item.title: Supply, demand to dominate market dynamics in 2026
item.description: While broader economic risks remain, market dynamics are being driven by supply, demand and income generation, rather than macro headlines, said Pat Haskell, head of the municipal bond group at BlackRock.
